obligations.description: Fixed complete system and software domain
obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Run the complete system from reset through the end of the firmware, keeping the external input variable.
obligations.expected: The top level for this task is the complete five-stage pipelined pipelined_riscv_core, with fixed WIDTH=32 and PROGRAM_FILE="program3.hex"; replacing the program is not allowed. ROM and RAM each contain 256 32-bit words, and unlisted portions of ROM are NOPs. The public program table defines the software domain for this task; support for arbitrary RV32I programs need not be guaranteed. Use only known two-state inputs.
obligations.sampling: Edge numbering starts at edge 1 after reset release; inputs are stable before the rising edge, and comparison is performed 1ns after the edge; after a falling reset edge, an additional comparison is performed before the next clock.
obligations.checker: Predict valid/data independently from reset and input history; compare all outputs using four-state comparisons after every clock edge, issuing UVM_ERROR on a mismatch; also compare between reset edges. Count complete result events, cancellations, and comparisons; passing without activity is prohibited.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Apply reset separately at power-up, before and after sampling, before and after output, and during prolonged idle periods, including short pulses that do not span a rising edge and low levels spanning multiple clocks.
obligations.expected: i_rstn is an active-low asynchronous reset; its falling edge immediately clears result_valid and result_data, and clears the pipeline, PC, registers, and RAM. Generate at least one actual falling reset edge; all outputs are 0 during reset. Release reset away from a rising clock edge; the next rising edge counts as edge 1.

Count complete result events, cancellations, and comparisons; passing without activity is prohibited.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Each legal run starts from a fresh reset; change the input before and after the sampling window, and use multiple resets to verify that old RAM and register state does not leak.
obligations.expected: Byte address fffffff8 is read-only input_data, and fffffffc is the result register; neither writes ordinary RAM. The datapath uses 32-bit whole-word reads and writes, and the ordinary RAM word index is the byte address shifted right by 2. The fixed firmware accesses only RAM word 0, writing before reading; there is no externally modifiable code or memory port.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Use mutually distinct patterns at edges 20, 21, and 22, and keep changing the input at other edges; cover constant inputs and inputs that change every cycle.
obligations.expected: On the 21st rising edge of i_clk after each reset release, sample input_data as the 32-bit unsigned bit vector for this transaction; it must be stable before the edge and held through that edge. Inputs at other times do not affect this result. A run canceled by reset before sampling produces no result; each run samples only once.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Inputs cover 0, fffffffb, fffffffc, ffffffff, 7fffffff, 80000000, alternating bits, single-set-bit patterns, and random 32-bit values.
obligations.expected: The firmware sets x8=-8, reads input_data into x9, computes x10=x9+7, writes RAM word 0 and reads it back into x11, computes x11=x11-3, and writes the result address; all operations are truncated to 32 bits modulo 2^32. Thus, the result is the input at edge 21 plus 4 modulo 2^32; saturation or signed truncation must not be used.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: For a complete run, observe edges 65, 66, and 67 and at least several hundred later cycles; also reset after edge 65 to verify that no delayed output occurs.
obligations.expected: If reset does not interrupt the run, after the 66th rising edge result_valid is 1 and result_data updates to this run's result; result_valid is 0 at edges 1 through 65, and is 0 at edge 67 and thereafter. Only one single-cycle pulse is produced even if the input remains unchanged. After the rising edge, wait for nonblocking assignments to settle before observing.

Count complete result events, cancellations, and comparisons; passing without activity is prohibited.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Continue changing the input after the result and run for hundreds of cycles, comparing every cycle that data holds and valid is 0; then reset and rerun with a different input.
obligations.expected: result_data remains 0 after reset until the first result, and continuously holds the result after updating at edge 66, including all edges where result_valid is 0; only the next reset clears it to zero. The JAL self-loop at the end of the firmware does not write the result again and does not repeat the output in response to subsequent input_data changes. Both result_valid and result_data are public state valid on every cycle.

obligations.setup: After a real reset falling edge, release reset on a falling edge.
obligations.stimulus: Cancel after edges 20, 21, 65, 66, and 67 separately, alternate short/long resets, and restart with mutually distinct inputs to confirm that old samples are not mixed in.
obligations.expected: An effective reset at any time cancels the old run, without queuing or reissuing the old result; after release, timing restarts from edge 1. This includes reset after sampling but before output, immediately after edge 66, and during a prolonged trailing loop. The new result comes only from the input at edge 21 of the new run.
